text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. REST APIs are a popular choice because they use simple HTTP methods like GET and POST. Each endpoint should represent one clear resource, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct status codes so clients understand what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Clear documentation helps developers learn your API quickly, so write it carefully. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, to add new features without breaking existing applications. Following these practices saves time and prevents confusion.
